chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Kulayb ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: It is not befitting for the believer that he becomes estranged from his brother who is below him. The believer is highly valued in his religion.'

key_terms.أَخِيهِ: his brother — denoting the bond of brotherhood between believers rooted in shared iman
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer — one who possesses true iman (faith), the subject of the Imam's teaching
key_terms.دُونَهُ: below him — one of lesser religious understanding, knowledge, or spiritual station
key_terms.دِينِهِ: his religion — Islam as the very source and ground of the believer's honor and worth
key_terms.عَزِيزٌ: highly valued, noble, and honorable — the intrinsic dignity conferred upon the believer by his religion
key_terms.يَسْتَوْحِشَ: to become estranged, to feel aversion or alienation toward another — here signifying the act of withdrawing from or looking down upon a fellow believer

ai.seo_question: Should a believer distance himself from fellow believers who are below him in religious understanding?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) via Kulayb ibn Mu'awiyah, teaches that a believer must not distance himself or feel estranged from his fellow believer who is of lesser understanding or spiritual standing. It concludes by affirming the inherent honor and dignity that every believer carries by virtue of his religion, implying that this shared nobility is a sufficient basis for solidarity and brotherhood.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Kuleyb Bin Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I heard himasws saying: ‘It is not befitting for the Momin that he alienates to his brother from the ones below him (in understanding). The Momineen are highly valued people in their Religion’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Kulayb ibn Mu’awiyah who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘
It does not benefit a believer to be apprehensive of his brother (in belief) of less perfect belief; believers are highly valued people in their religion.’”
